public_rationale: Bloomberg's February 24, 2025 report described canceled US leases totaling “a couple of hundred megawatts” and reduced conversion of preliminary agreements into leases [e1]. Bisnow's March 27 report cited a March 26 estimate of 2 GW of abandoned pending leases over six months, a period extending beyond March 3 [e2]. The April 28 account identified the reported 2 GW as nonbinding letters of intent but did not establish how much had been abandoned by March 3 [e3]. These reports establish neither a nonduplicated total substantially above 1 GW by publication nor an upper bound that contradicts the claim [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The reports do not provide project-level dates and capacity figures sufficient to remove overlap and separate abandonment from temporary deferral [e1, e2, e3].
The later 2 GW estimate cannot be assigned wholly to the period ending March 3, 2025 [e2, e3].

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that the capacity Microsoft had already abandoned substantially exceeded one gigawatt by March 3, 2025.

The surrounding post includes canceled leases, expired letters of intent, abandoned negotiations and land deals. The claim therefore concerns abandoned planned capacity, not exclusively terminated binding leases.
The target is the cumulative abandonment described as of publication. Its beginning is unspecified; no arbitrary starting date is imposed.
Substantially higher requires a material excess over one gigawatt. The speaker supplied no numerical multiplier.
Later reporting can establish earlier cancellations, but cancellations occurring after publication cannot establish this observation.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reporting or project records establish a nonduplicated total of abandoned planned capacity substantially above one gigawatt by March 3, 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive accounting establishes that the abandoned capacity by March 3, 2025 was at or below one gigawatt, or exceeded it only marginally.
